36 divided by 6 is 6, because 6 times 6 is 36.
Put that answer where the box was. Now the sum is 6 plus 14.
6 plus 14 is 20.
Notice something funny. The answer to the divide was also a 6. But the first job was still the divide, not the plus.
So: divide before you add.
Let us multiply 2 by 4.
2 times 4 means 2 groups of 4. Picture 2 rows with 4 in each row.
Which adding sum shows 2 groups of 4?

ask.ifNot: 2 groups of 4 means the 4 is written 2 times, with plus signs in between.

beats.say: Add them up. 4 plus 4 makes 8.
So 2 times 4 is 8.
We can turn it round as well. 4 groups of 2 also make 8.
So times is a quick way of adding the same number again and again.
A bracket, a divide and a times. We take them in order.
Bracket first. 4 plus 4 is 8.
Now a divide and a times are left. Which goes first?

ask.ifNot: Divide and times are equal partners, so we go left to right. The divide is on the left, so it goes first.

beats.say: Divide and times are equal partners, so we go left to right, like reading. 48 divided by 8 is 6.
Then 6 times 2 is 12.
Two things to watch. Use the whole bracket, 8, not just one of the 4s. And do not stop at 6: the times 2 is still waiting.
So: brackets first. Then divide and times from left to right.
Look at the signs here. A minus, then a times, then a plus.
So, which bit goes first?

ask.ifNot: It is tempting to start on the left. But multiplying always goes first, so 7 times 2 is our first job.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 7 times 2.
7 times 2 is 14. So 14 goes where the box was. The rest of the sum stays the same.
Just a minus and a plus now. Which one comes first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 23 take away 14.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 23 take away 14 is 9.
One job left, the plus. 9 and 10 make 19.
Did you spot the trap? Going left to right from the very start would mean taking away before multiplying, and that gives a different number.
The rule: multiply first. Then add and take away in order, from left to right.
Look at the signs here. A minus, then a times, then a plus.
Where do we begin?

ask.ifNot: Times goes before plus and minus, even when it sits in the middle. So we begin with 8 times 3.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 8 times 3.
8 times 3 is 24. So 24 goes where the box was. The rest of the sum stays the same.
Just a minus and a plus now. Which one comes first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 36 take away 24.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 36 take away 24 is 12.
One job left, the plus. 12 and 9 make 21.
The trap in this sum is the minus at the front. It looks like the place to start, but the times must go first.
The rule: multiply first. Then add and take away in order, from left to right.
Three kinds of bracket, tucked inside each other like nesting dolls. We start with the smallest doll, in the middle.
Which bracket is in the very middle?

ask.ifNot: The round bracket is the innermost one. So we start with 3 plus 2.

beats.say: Round bracket first. 3 plus 2 is 5.
Next, the curly bracket. 10 take away 5 is 5.
Careful here. Only that 5 is taken away from 25. We do not take away the 10, and then the 5 as well.
Last, the square bracket. 25 take away 5 is 20.
So with brackets inside brackets, work from the inside out: round, then curly, then square.
Here is a sum with fractions: one half, plus one third times 6. The order rules work just the same.
Which part goes first?

ask.ifNot: Times goes before plus, with fractions too. So one third times 6 comes first.

beats.say: Times goes first. One third times 6 means one third of 6. So share 6 into 3 equal groups.
6 divided by 3 is 2. So one third of 6 is 2.
Now the sum is one half plus 2. That makes 2 and a half.
The choices are written as decimals. One half is the same as 0.5. So 2 and a half is 2.5.
The trap is adding the half and the third first. The 6 multiplies only the one third, so that job is done first.
So the answer is 2.5. Times before plus, even with fractions.
A minus, a divide and a times. The minus is first in line, but it is not the first job to be done.
Which sign has to wait until the end?

ask.ifNot: Divide and times go before minus. So the minus waits until the end.

beats.say: Divide and times go before minus. So box the middle part: 50 divided by 5 times 2.
Inside the box there is a divide and a times. Which goes first?

ask.ifNot: Divide and times are equal partners, so we go left to right. 50 divided by 5 comes first.

beats.say: Left to right. 50 divided by 5 is 10. Then 10 times 2 is 20.
So the box is worth 20. Now the minus gets its turn.
100 take away 20 is 80.
The trap is starting with 100 take away 50, just because it is on the left. And 20 is not the final answer: it still has to be taken from 100.
So: divide and times first, from left to right. Then the minus.
Here is our sum. It has three signs in it: a minus, a times and a plus.
Which part do we work out first?

ask.ifNot: Times goes before plus and minus, even when it sits in the middle. So we begin with 2 times 5.

beats.say: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So we box the 2 times 5. It goes first.
2 times 5 is 10. So 10 goes where the box was. The rest of the sum stays the same.
Now only a minus and a plus are left. Which do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 17 take away 10.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 17 take away 10 is 7.
And now the plus. 7 plus 1 is 8.
The trap in this sum is the minus at the front. It looks like the place to start, but the times must go first.
The rule: multiply first. Then add and take away in order, from left to right.
Three signs in one sum: a minus, a times and a plus. The trick is knowing where to start.
So, which bit goes first?

ask.ifNot: It is tempting to start on the left. But multiplying always goes first, so 6 times 4 is our first job.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 6 times 4.
6 times 4 is 24. Write 24 in its place, and copy everything else just as it was.
Now only a minus and a plus are left. Which do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 47 take away 24.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 47 take away 24 is 23.
And now the plus. 23 plus 8 is 31.
The trap in this sum is the minus at the front. It looks like the place to start, but the times must go first.
So remember: times first, then plus and minus from left to right.
Three signs in one sum: a minus, a times and a plus. The trick is knowing where to start.
Which part do we work out first?

ask.ifNot: It is tempting to start on the left. But multiplying always goes first, so 5 times 9 is our first job.

beats.say: Multiplying goes before adding and taking away. So we box the 5 times 9. It goes first.
5 times 9 is 45. So 45 goes where the box was. The rest of the sum stays the same.
Now only a minus and a plus are left. Which do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 45 take away 45.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 45 take away 45 leaves nothing at all. That is 0.
And now the plus. 0 plus 15 is 15.
Did you spot the trap? Going left to right from the very start would mean taking away before multiplying, and that gives a different number.
So remember: times first, then plus and minus from left to right.
The word estimate means we do not need the exact answer. We want a quick, sensible answer, using friendly round numbers.
498 is very close to a friendly round number. Which one?

ask.ifNot: 498 is only 2 away from 500. So we round it to 500.

beats.say: 498 is just 2 less than 500. So we use 500.
And 21 is just 1 more than 20. So we use 20.
Now multiply the round numbers. 5 times 2 is 10. Then put the three zeros back: two from 500 and one from 20.
So our estimate is 10,000.
Careful with the trap. Round both numbers, not just one. If only the 498 is rounded, the estimate comes out too high.
So to estimate, round each number to a friendly one, then multiply.
Here is a times sum that has been split into two easier pieces. One number is missing, and we must find it.
35 times 12 means 12 lots of 35. Someone has split those 12 lots into 10 lots, and some more lots.
10 lots are already there. How many more lots do we need to make 12 lots?

ask.ifNot: 12 is 10 and 2 more. The 10 lots are already there, so 2 more lots are needed.

beats.say: 12 is 10 and 2. So 12 lots is 10 lots and 2 lots.
So the missing number is 2.
We can check. 35 times 10 is 350, and 35 times 2 is 70. 350 plus 70 is 420, which is 35 times 12.
So a big times sum can be split into two small ones. The two pieces must add up to the number you started with. Here, 10 and 2 make 12.
This one looks big, but there is nothing to work out. It is asking about a rule of multiplying.
Try a small one first. 3 times 4 is 12. And 4 times 3 is 12 as well. The order does not matter.
Picture 3 rows of 4 squares. Turn the page sideways and it is 4 rows of 3 squares. Same squares, same number.
Now look at our sum. The left side is 256 times 18. The right side starts with 18. So which number is missing?

ask.ifNot: The two numbers have simply swapped places. 18 is already there, so the missing one is 256.

beats.say: The two numbers have just swapped places. So the missing number is 256.
Did you notice? We never had to multiply 256 by 18 at all.
So remember: you can multiply two numbers in either order, and the answer is the same.
Four signs in one line: divide, times, minus and plus. Let us sort out the order.
Which chunk is done first?

ask.ifNot: Divide and times go before minus and plus. So the first chunk, 72 divided by 8 times 3, is done first.

beats.say: Divide and times go first. Box that chunk.
Inside the box we go left to right. 72 divided by 8 is 9. Then 9 times 3 is 27.
Now the sum is 27 minus 6 plus 4.
27 is not the final answer. Two jobs are left. Which comes first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go left to right. 27 take away 6 comes first.

beats.say: 27 take away 6 is 21. Then 21 plus 4 is 25.
The trap is adding the 6 and the 4 together first. Only the 6 is taken away. The 4 is added.
So: divide and times from left to right, then minus and plus from left to right.
5 pens cost 35 rupees. We want the cost of 8 pens.
We cannot jump straight from 5 pens to 8 pens. What should we find first?

ask.ifNot: Once we know the cost of 1 pen, we can find the cost of any number of pens.

beats.say: Find the cost of one pen. Share 35 rupees among 5 pens. 35 divided by 5 is 7.
So one pen costs 7 rupees.
Now 8 pens at 7 rupees each. Which sum do we need?

ask.ifNot: Each of the 8 pens costs 7 rupees. So we need 8 lots of 7.

beats.say: 8 times 7 is 56. So 8 pens cost 56 rupees.
Does it make sense? 8 pens are more than 5 pens, so they should cost more than 35 rupees. And 56 is more. Good.
So: find the cost of one first, then multiply by how many you want.
Two sides with an equals sign between them. The brackets have moved, and one number has gone missing.
Look at the left side. It multiplies three numbers: 12, 5 and 4.
The right side must multiply the same three numbers. It already shows 12 and 5. Which one is missing?

ask.ifNot: The left side uses 12, 5 and 4. The right side shows 12 and 5. So the 4 is missing.

beats.say: The 4 is missing.
Let us check both sides. On the left, 12 times 5 is 60, and 60 times 4 is 240.
On the right, 5 times 4 is 20, and 12 times 20 is 240. The same!
So when you multiply three numbers, you can group them any way you like. The answer stays the same, and the missing number is 4.
This sum is meant to equal 36. Let us see what it gives now, and whether brackets can fix it.
With no brackets, times goes first. 4 times 3 is 12, and 8 plus 12 is 20. Not 36.
We need a bigger answer. Which job should we make happen first?

ask.ifNot: 4 times 3 already goes first, and that gave 20. So try making 8 plus 4 go first instead.

beats.say: Brackets make a job go first. Put them round 8 plus 4.
Brackets first. 8 plus 4 is 12.
Then 12 times 3 is 36. That is our number!
So the brackets go round 8 plus 4.
Brackets round 4 times 3 would change nothing, because times goes first anyway. Brackets only help when they change the order.
Two gaps, and each needs a sign. The answer must be 9. We test the choices.
Try plus then minus. 12 plus 4 is 16, and 16 take away 3 is 13. Not 9.
Try times then minus. 12 times 4 is 48, and 48 take away 3 is 45. Far too big.
Now try divide then times: 12 divided by 4 times 3. Which goes first?

ask.ifNot: Divide and times are equal partners, so we go left to right. 12 divided by 4 comes first.

beats.say: Left to right. 12 divided by 4 is 3. Then 3 times 3 is 9. That is our number!
So the signs are divide, then times.
Careful with the trap. Doing 4 times 3 first would give 12 divided by 12, which is 1. With divide and times, go left to right.
So test each pair of signs, and always follow the order rules.
999 times 7 looks like hard work. But 999 has a very friendly neighbour.
Which round number is just 1 more than 999?

ask.ifNot: 999 plus 1 is 1,000. And 1,000 is very easy to multiply.

beats.say: 999 is 1 less than 1,000. So start with 1,000 lots of 7. That is 7,000.
But 1,000 lots is one lot too many. What do we take away?

ask.ifNot: We counted one extra lot of 7. So we take away 7, not 1.

beats.say: Take away one lot of 7. 7,000 take away 7 is 6,993.
So 999 times 7 is 6,993.
A quick check on the last digit. 9 times 7 is 63, which ends in 3. Our answer ends in 3 too.
So when a number is 1 less than a round number, use the round number, then take one lot away.
We divide 157 by 6 and want the remainder. That is what is left over after making as many groups of 6 as we can.
Build up in sixes. 6 times 10 is 60, so 6 times 20 is 120.
From 120 we still have 37 to go to reach 157.
How many sixes fit into 37?

ask.ifNot: Say the 6 times table. 6 sixes fit inside 37, but 7 sixes would be too many.

beats.say: 6 times 6 is 36. So altogether 26 sixes fit, and they make 156.
157 take away 156 leaves 1. So the remainder is 1.
A remainder is always smaller than the number you divide by. 1 is smaller than 6, so that fits.
So to find a remainder, find the biggest multiple that fits, then subtract. Here the remainder is 1.
Here is our sum. 64 times 38.
That is a big one, so we break it into two smaller jobs. Split 38 into 30 and 8.
Start with the tens piece, 30. First, 64 times 3. 60 times 3 is 180, and 4 times 3 is 12. Together that makes 192.
30 is 3 tens. So what is 64 times 30?

ask.ifNot: 30 is ten times 3. So the answer is ten times 192, which is 192 with a 0 on the end.

beats.say: Ten times 192 is 1920. That is the first piece done.
Now the ones piece. 64 times 8. 60 times 8 is 480, and 4 times 8 is 32. Together that makes 512.
Now put the two pieces together. 1920 and 512 make 2432.
So 64 times 38 equals 2432.
A quick check on the last digit. 4 times 8 is 32, which ends in 2. Our answer ends in 2 too.
Break it up, multiply each piece, add the pieces. Big sums are just small sums in a row.
Here is our sum. 44 take away 16. Look at the sign first. It is a minus, so we take away.
Taking away 16 in one go is hard. So split it into 10 and 6.
Take the tens away first. What is 44 take away 10?

ask.ifNot: Only the tens change. 4 tens take away 1 ten leaves 3 tens, and the 4 ones stay. That is 34.

beats.say: Only the tens change, and the ones stay. So we have 34.
Now take away the 6. Careful here: 34 has only 4 ones. So take 4 first, to land on 30.
6 is 4 and 2, so there are 2 more to take. 30 take away 2 is 28.
So 44 minus 16 is 28.
Check by adding back. 28 plus 16 makes 44, the number we started with.
Split the number you are taking away. Tens first, then ones.
25 times 4. Here is a neat trick: multiplying by 4 is the same as doubling, and then doubling again.
Why does that work? Because 4 is 2 times 2.
So first, double 25. What is 25 plus 25?

ask.ifNot: 2 tens doubled is 4 tens. 5 doubled is 10, which is one more ten. That makes 5 tens, and 5 tens is 50.

beats.say: Double 25 is 50.
Now double again. Double 50 is 100.
So 25 times 4 is 100.
This is a fact worth keeping in your head: four 25s make 100.
So to multiply by 4, double and double again.
Ria buys two kinds of things: notebooks and pens. We find the cost of each kind, then add.

board.text: 3 notebooks at 45 rupees.   2 pens at 12 rupees.

beats.say: Start with the notebooks. 3 notebooks at 45 rupees each. Which sum?

ask.ifNot: Each of the 3 notebooks costs 45 rupees. So we need 3 lots of 45.

beats.say: 3 times 45. 3 times 40 is 120, and 3 times 5 is 15. Together, 135 rupees.
Now the pens. 2 pens at 12 rupees each. 2 times 12 is 24 rupees.
We have 135 rupees for notebooks and 24 rupees for pens. What is the last step?

ask.ifNot: She paid for both the notebooks and the pens. So we add the two costs together.

beats.say: 135 plus 24 is 159. Ria spent 159 rupees.
We can write the whole story on one line. Times first, then the plus.
So: work out each kind of thing on its own, then add the costs. The total is 159 rupees.
1,000 divided by 8. Dividing by 8 sounds hard, but halving is easy. And 8 is made of halvings.
8 is 2 times 2 times 2. So dividing by 8 is the same as halving three times.
First halving. Half of 1,000 is 500.
Second halving. What is half of 500?

ask.ifNot: Half of 5 hundreds is 2 and a half hundreds. That is 250.

beats.say: Half of 500 is 250.
Third halving. Half of 250. Half of 200 is 100, and half of 50 is 25. Together, 125.
So 1,000 divided by 8 is 125.
Check. 8 times 100 is 800, and 8 times 25 is 200. Together that is 1,000. It fits.
So to divide by 8, halve, halve, and halve again. The answer is 125.
81 plus 6. Let us work it out together. Look at the sign first. It is a plus, so we add.
81 is 80 and 1. Let us split it into its tens and its ones.
There is room in the ones place, so only the ones will change. What is 1 plus 6?

ask.ifNot: Start at 1 and count on 6 more. You land on 7.

beats.say: 1 one and 6 ones make 7 ones.
The tens have not changed, so put them back. 80 and 7 make 87.
So 81 plus 6 equals 87.
Let us check by going backwards. 87 take away 6 brings us back to 81.
The plan: split off the ones, add the ones, then put the tens back.
This question is about a rule, not about one sum. What happens when any number is multiplied by 1?
Let us try a few. Multiplying by 1 means one group. One group of 6 is just 6.
Try another. What is 9 times 1?

ask.ifNot: 9 times 1 means one group of 9. One group of 9 is just 9.

beats.say: One group of 9 is 9. It works for bigger numbers too. One group of 45 is 45.
Look down the board. Each time, the answer is the very number we started with.
So any number multiplied by 1 gives the same number.
Do not mix it up with adding 1, which makes a number one bigger. Multiplying by 1 changes nothing at all.
Another rule question. What happens when any number is multiplied by 0?
Picture 4 plates with nothing on any of them. How many sweets altogether? None. So 4 times 0 is 0.
Try a bigger one. 100 plates, all empty. How many sweets?

ask.ifNot: Every plate is empty. However many empty plates you have, there are still no sweets at all.

beats.say: Still none. 100 times 0 is 0.
It never matters how big the number is. Lots of nothing is still nothing.
So any number multiplied by 0 gives 0.
Do not mix it up with multiplying by 1, which gives the same number back. Multiplying by 0 always gives 0.
A chain of four instructions. We follow them one at a time, in order, and keep track on the board.
Start with 5. Double it. 5 times 2 is 10.
Add 3. 10 plus 3 is 13.
Now multiply by 4. Which number do we multiply?

ask.ifNot: Each instruction works on the newest number in the chain. Right now that is 13.

beats.say: 13 times 4. 10 times 4 is 40, and 3 times 4 is 12. Together, 52.
Is 52 the answer?

ask.ifNot: There is one more instruction in the chain: subtract 2.

beats.say: Last step. 52 take away 2 is 50.
So in a chain like this, do every step in order, each on the newest number, and do not stop early.
Three signs in one sum: a minus, a times and a plus. The trick is knowing where to start.
Which part do we work out first?

ask.ifNot: It is tempting to start on the left. But multiplying always goes first, so 4 times 7 is our first job.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 4 times 7.
4 times 7 is 28. So 28 goes where the box was. The rest of the sum stays the same.
Just a minus and a plus now. Which one comes first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 37 take away 28.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 37 take away 28 is 9.
And now the plus. 9 plus 3 is 12.
Did you spot the trap? Going left to right from the very start would mean taking away before multiplying, and that gives a different number.
The rule: multiply first. Then add and take away in order, from left to right.
Here is our sum. It has three signs in it: a minus, a times and a plus.
Which part do we work out first?

ask.ifNot: It is tempting to start on the left. But multiplying always goes first, so 2 times 2 is our first job.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 2 times 2.
2 times 2 is 4. So 4 goes where the box was. The rest of the sum stays the same.
Now only a minus and a plus are left. Which do we do first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 14 take away 4.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 14 take away 4 is 10.
One job left, the plus. 10 and 14 make 24.
Did you spot the trap? Going left to right from the very start would mean taking away before multiplying, and that gives a different number.
The rule: multiply first. Then add and take away in order, from left to right.
Here is our sum. It has three signs in it: a minus, a times and a plus.
Which part do we work out first?

ask.ifNot: It is tempting to start on the left. But multiplying always goes first, so 6 times 3 is our first job.

beats.say: Times is the boss here. It goes before plus and minus, so put a box round 6 times 3.
6 times 3 is 18. Write 18 in its place, and copy everything else just as it was.
Just a minus and a plus now. Which one comes first?

ask.ifNot: Plus and minus are equal partners, so we go from left to right, just like reading. The minus comes first: 42 take away 18.

beats.say: Left to right, just like reading. 42 take away 18 is 24.
One job left, the plus. 24 and 7 make 31.
Did you spot the trap? Going left to right from the very start would mean taking away before multiplying, and that gives a different number.
So remember: times first, then plus and minus from left to right.
7 times some number makes 91. We need to find that hidden number.
Which sum finds the hidden number?

ask.ifNot: 7 equal groups make 91. To find the size of one group, we divide 91 by 7.

beats.say: Divide undoes times. So we need 91 divided by 7.
Split 91 into two friendly pieces: 70 and 21. Both are in the 7 times table.
70 divided by 7 is 10. And 21 divided by 7 is 3.
10 and 3 make 13. So the hidden number is 13.
Check by multiplying. 7 times 13 is 91. It fits.
So to find a missing number in a times sum, divide. Here it is 13.
Let us add 50 and 42.
50 is a round number, full tens and no ones. So we only need to split the 42, into 40 and 2.
Add the tens first. What is 50 plus 40?

ask.ifNot: 5 tens and 4 tens make 9 tens. And 9 tens is 90.

beats.say: 5 tens and 4 tens make 9 tens. That is 90.
Now bring in the 2 ones. 90 and 2 make 92.
There it is. 50 plus 42 makes 92.
A quick check. 92 take away 42 is 50, right where we started. It fits.
So add the tens first, then drop the ones in.
Let us take 8 away from 82.
82 has only 2 ones, and we need to take away 8. So first take away 2, to land on the round number 80.
We have taken 2 so far, out of 8. How many more do we still have to take away?

ask.ifNot: 8 is 2 and 6. We have taken the 2, so 6 more are still to go.

beats.say: 8 is 2 and 6. The 2 is done, and the 6 is still waiting.
Now hop back 6 more from 80. That lands on 74.
So 82 take away 8 equals 74.
Check by adding back. 74 plus 8 makes 82, the number we started with.
The plan: go back to the round ten first, then take away the rest.
Let us multiply 97 by 46. Look at the sign first. It is times, so we multiply.
That is a big one, so we break it into two smaller jobs. Split 46 into 40 and 6.
Start with the tens piece, 40. First, 97 times 4. 90 times 4 is 360, and 7 times 4 is 28. Together that makes 388.
40 is 4 tens. So what is 97 times 40?

ask.ifNot: 40 is ten times 4. So the answer is ten times 388, which is 388 with a 0 on the end.

beats.say: Ten times 388 is 3880. That is the first piece done.
Now the ones piece. 97 times 6. 90 times 6 is 540, and 7 times 6 is 42. Together that makes 582.
Add the two pieces. 3880 plus 582 is 4462.
So 97 times 46 equals 4462.
A quick check on the last digit. 7 times 6 is 42, which ends in 2. Our answer ends in 2 too.
Break it up, multiply each piece, add the pieces. Big sums are just small sums in a row.
Here is our sum. 3 times 2. Look at the sign first. It is times, so we multiply.
3 times 2 means 3 groups of 2. Picture 3 rows with 2 in each row.
Which adding sum shows 3 groups of 2?

ask.ifNot: 3 groups of 2 means the 2 is written 3 times, with plus signs in between.

beats.say: Add them up. 2 plus 2 plus 2 makes 6.
There it is. 3 times 2 makes 6.
We can turn it round as well. 2 groups of 3 also make 6.
So times is a quick way of adding the same number again and again.
Here is our sum. 4 plus 11.
Adding works in any order. So let us start from the bigger number, 11, and add the 4 to it.
11 is 10 and 1. Let us split it into its tens and its ones.
There is room in the ones place, so only the ones will change. What is 1 plus 4?

ask.ifNot: Start at 1 and count on 4 more. You land on 5.

beats.say: 1 one and 4 ones make 5 ones.
The tens have not changed, so put them back. 10 and 5 make 15.
So 4 plus 11 equals 15.
Let us check by going backwards. 15 take away 11 brings us back to 4.
So when you add a small number and there is room in the ones, keep the tens and just add the ones.
Here is our sum. 86 times 12. The sign is times, so we want 86 lots of 12, not 86 plus 12.
Too big to do in one go. So split 12 into 10 and 2, and do one piece at a time.
First, 86 times 10. That is 860, the same digits with a 0 on the end.
We split 12 into 10 and 2. The 10 is done. What is still left to multiply 86 by?

ask.ifNot: 12 is 10 and 2. We have done the 10, so the 2 is still left.

beats.say: Now the ones piece. 86 times 2. 80 times 2 is 160, and 6 times 2 is 12. Together that makes 172.
Now put the two pieces together. 860 and 172 make 1032.
So 86 times 12 equals 1032.
A quick check on the last digit. 6 times 2 is 12, which ends in 2. Our answer ends in 2 too.
Break it up, multiply each piece, add the pieces. Big sums are just small sums in a row.
Here is our sum. 14 take away 4.
14 is 10 and 4. Let us split it into its tens and its ones.
There are enough ones to take 4 from. So only the ones change. What is 4 take away 4?

ask.ifNot: Start at 4 and hop back 4. You land on 0.

beats.say: 4 ones take away 4 ones leaves no ones at all.
The tens have not changed, so put them back. 10 and 0 make 10.
There it is. 14 minus 4 leaves 10.
Let us check by going backwards. 10 plus 4 is 14. It fits.
So when there are enough ones, keep the tens and just take away from the ones.
Let us take 48 away from 88. Look at the sign first. It is a minus, so we take away.
Taking away 48 in one go is hard. So split it into 40 and 8.
Take the tens away first. What is 88 take away 40?

ask.ifNot: Only the tens change. 8 tens take away 4 tens leaves 4 tens, and the 8 ones stay. That is 48.

beats.say: Only the tens change, and the ones stay. So we have 48.
Now take away the 8 ones. 48 take away 8 is 40.
So 88 minus 48 is 40.
Check by adding back. 40 plus 48 makes 88, the number we started with.
So the plan is: take away the tens first, then take away the ones.
28 times 36. Let us work it out together.
Too big to do in one go. So split 36 into 30 and 6, and do one piece at a time.
Start with the tens piece, 30. First, 28 times 3. 20 times 3 is 60, and 8 times 3 is 24. Together that makes 84.
30 is 3 tens. So what is 28 times 30?

ask.ifNot: 30 is ten times 3. So the answer is ten times 84, which is 84 with a 0 on the end.

beats.say: Ten times 84 is 840. That is the first piece done.
Now the ones piece. 28 times 6. 20 times 6 is 120, and 8 times 6 is 48. Together that makes 168.
Now put the two pieces together. 840 and 168 make 1008.
So 28 times 36 equals 1008.
A quick check on the last digit. 8 times 6 is 48, which ends in 8. Our answer ends in 8 too.
So the plan is: split one number into tens and ones, multiply each piece, then add.
81 plus 48. Let us work it out together. Look at the sign first. It is a plus, so we add.
Big numbers are friendlier in pieces. So we split each one into its tens and its ones.
Start with the tens. What is 80 plus 40?

ask.ifNot: 8 tens and 4 tens make 12 tens. And 12 tens is 120.

beats.say: 8 tens and 4 tens make 12 tens. That is 120.
Now the ones. 1 plus 8 is 9.
Last, join the two parts. 120 plus 9 is 129.
So 81 plus 48 equals 129.
Let us check by going backwards. 129 take away 48 brings us back to 81.

Put each answer where its box was, with the plus still in between.
Now the plus gets its turn. 5 plus 30 is 35.
The trap here is going straight along from left to right. The 5 must not be added until the times is done.
So remember: divide and multiply first, then add.
